comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose their reportable segment structures, but they differ significantly in the number of segments and business composition. Broadcom reports two segments (semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software), explicitly separating its software business which AMD does not do in its segment definitions. AMD reports four segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) focused primarily on hardware and accelerators. Broadcom's disclosure highlights its dual nature of semiconductors and software, whereas AMD's disclosure focuses on its diverse hardware portfolio across compute, client, gaming, and embedded markets.

sentences.text: We have two reportable segments: semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software.

comparisons.peer_summary: Business is organized into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All other; CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry are reportable operating segments, while NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable segments with selective disclosure.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose their reportable segment designations, though Intel's structure is more complex with explicit distinctions between reportable and non-reportable segments. Intel identifies three reportable operating segments (CCG, DCAI, Intel Foundry) and explicitly notes that NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable, whereas Broadcom simply states it has two reportable segments (semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software) without detailing non-reportable entities in this specific sentence. Both companies organize their reporting to align with how the chief operating decision maker reviews the business.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition of Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU)
comparisons.peer_summary: The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
comparisons.comparison: While Broadcom discloses broad reportable segments covering both semiconductors and infrastructure software, Micron discloses specific business units within its memory and storage focus. Micron's Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU) is defined by the markets it serves (data center, PC, graphics, networking) rather than a specific technology type like semiconductors vs software. This contrasts with Broadcom's broader segmentation which separates hardware solutions from software solutions, indicating a different organizational focus on product type vs. application market.
